# `ms` command reference

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen_skill_reference.py from the Typer command tree: do not edit by hand. `uv run python scripts/gen_skill_reference.py` rewrites it; tests/skill/ fails when it drifts. -->

Every command accepts `--json` and then prints exactly one line, `{"ok": true, "data": ...}` or `{"ok": false, "error": {"code", "message", "alternative"}}`, plus `"next_command"` when one `ms` command resolves the refusal (UPPER-CASE words in it are blanks to fill in). Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 unexpected, 2 usage, 3 refused, 4 blocked, 5 integrity. Run through `mise run ms -- <command>` so `op run` supplies credentials.

Global flag: `--version`.

## `ms adjust item`

Bind a one-off rule to one boi; prints who bears it before and after.

Side effects: WRITES the ledger: appends one one-off `rule.added` per slot, pinned to the boi, and recomputes the boi's and the period's client/AAI totals before and after in the same transaction. It can never change a vendor amount.

| flag | type | required | help |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--id` | str | yes | The boi id, or a unique prefix of 8+ hex characters. |
| `--bill-to` | one of: client, aai | no | Who bears this boi: client or aai. |
| `--split-cap` | int | no | AAI bears the first N cents. |
| `--split-bps` | int | no | AAI bears this share in bps (0-10000). |
| `--margin` | int | no | Flat cents added to the client-borne amount (35000 = USD 350.00). |
| `--margin-bps` | int | no | Percentage margin in basis points. |
| `--reason` | str | no | Why (recorded with the rule and actor). |
| `--json` | flag | no | Print one JSON line: {"ok": true, "data": ...} or an error. |

`--json` data:

`AdjustItemResult`:
- `boi_id`: str
- `scope_key`: str
- `client`: str
- `vendor`: str
- `period_start`: date
- `period_end`: date
- `rules`: list[AddedAdjustment]
- `reason`: str | null
- `before`: BoiAmounts
- `after`: BoiAmounts
- `period_before`: PeriodTotals
- `period_after`: PeriodTotals
- `after_trace`: list[str]
- `notes`: list[str]

## `ms audit`

Review a client and period for anomalies and recoveries; propose ms commands, run none. `ms audit feedback` records your verdict on a finding.

Side effects: A review of one client and period: it reports findings (each with an id, kind, severity, evidence, rationale and PROPOSED `ms` command lines) and runs none of them (`executed` is always false). Proposals are validated against the generated command tree; unknown commands or flags, another client, `--apply` and verdicts are dropped and listed under `dropped_proposals`. Read-only and offline by default: the deterministic checks (month-over-month spikes, missing, stale and provisional readings, leakage, unallocated shared cost, manual entries without evidence, dead rules, zombie subscriptions, a billable LLM vendor beside the gateway, AAI-borne cost by default, a closed month with no statement, an overdue Yrd, money left on the table (a margin below the pricing policy with the exact `ms rule add margin`, or the contract change for a client that forbids markup; a retainer allowance over- or under-used three closed months running), and cash versus accrual from the cached Mercury read only) need no network. `--llm` also sends the operator view (query outputs only) to `https://api.automaticai.io` with the per-consumer token `MILKSHAKE_AUDIT_LLM_TOKEN` (run through `mise run ms --`); what the model cites must exist in the ledger. A model pass (or `--record`) appends one `audit.completed`, with the prompt and every reply (a reply with no usable JSON is asked again, counted in `attempts` and archived too) as evidence blobs and every finding shown, and changes no billing state. A model pass whose record still meets `LEDGER_BUSY` after three polled waits is never dropped: it is kept under `$MILKSHAKE_HOME/runtime/audit-unrecorded/` (`unrecorded_archive`, and a note). Findings the operator rejected earlier are listed under `suppressed`, accepted ones that cleared under `resolved`. Refused: `LEDGER_READONLY` for `--llm` under `MILKSHAKE_READONLY` (before any request; run without `--llm`), `AUDIT_LLM_UNCONFIGURED`, `AUDIT_LLM_TOKEN_INVALID`, `AUDIT_LLM_REJECTED`, `AUDIT_LLM_UNAVAILABLE`, `AUDIT_LLM_REPLY_INVALID` (nothing is recorded).

| flag | type | required | help |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--client` | str | no | Client slug. |
| `--period` | str | no | Calendar month YYYY-MM (UTC). |
| `--from` | str | no | Range start YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `--to` | str | no | Range end YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. |
| `--at` | str | no | Judge staleness and overdue at this RFC 3339 instant. |
| `--llm` | flag | no | Also ask the gateway model to review the operator view (needs MILKSHAKE_AUDIT_LLM_TOKEN; archived on the ledger). |
| `--record` | flag | no | Record this run on the ledger so its ids can be answered. |
| `--json` | flag | no | Print one JSON line: {"ok": true, "data": ...} or an error. |

`--json` data:

`AuditReport`:
- `client`: str
- `period_start`: date
- `period_end`: date
- `as_of_seq`: int
- `now`: datetime
- `engine`: str
- `readiness`: Readiness
- `findings`: list[Finding]
- `suppressed`: list[Finding]
- `resolved`: list[Resolved]
- `counts`: dict[str, int]
- `notes`: list[str]
- `dropped_proposals`: list[str]
- `decisions`: list[PriorVerdict]
- `history`: list[HistoryRow]
- `llm`: LlmSummary | null
- `recorded_seq`: int | null
- `unrecorded_archive`: str | null
- `executed`: bool

## `ms audit feedback`

Record accept or reject for a finding; it is never executed. The next audit uses it.

Side effects: WRITES the ledger: appends one `audit.feedback` (accept or reject, with a required reason and your actor) for one finding's fingerprint; a repeat of the verdict in force appends nothing. **Accepting does not execute the proposal** (`executed` is always false). The next `ms audit` suppresses a rejected finding and keeps an accepted one visible until it clears. Refused: `AUDIT_FINDING_UNKNOWN`, `AUDIT_FINDING_AMBIGUOUS`, `REASON_REQUIRED`.

| flag | type | required | help |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--finding` | str | yes | The finding id an audit printed (F-xxxxxxxx). |
| `--decision` | one of: accept, reject | yes | accept or reject. |
| `--reason` | str | yes | Why (recorded on the ledger with the actor). |
| `--client` | str | no | With --period: find a plain run's finding again. |
| `--period` | str | no | Calendar month YYYY-MM of the audit. |
| `--json` | flag | no | Print one JSON line: {"ok": true, "data": ...} or an error. |

`--json` data:

`AuditFeedbackResult`:
- `finding_id`: str
- `fingerprint`: str
- `kind`: str
- `source`: str
- `client`: str
- `decision`: Decision
- `reason`: str
- `seq`: int | null
- `changed`: bool
- `executed`: bool
- `proposed_commands`: list[str]
- `effect`: str

## `ms boi fetch`

Fetch an API-less vendor's invoice for a month. A plan unless --apply is given.

Side effects: PLAN by default: lists the browser steps and, per manual row of the vendor, the prefilled `ms boi add --manual` that stays the way out; opens no browser and appends nothing. Only a vendor with a fetcher (Cartesia) can be fetched. With `--apply` it drives the Kapture capability (`MILKSHAKE_KAPTURE_URL`, default `http://127.0.0.1:61822`: a new tab of the operator's signed-in Chrome, closed afterwards) before the ledger transaction opens, downloads the invoice documents the page links without the browser's cookies or session, reads each one's invoice number, total and service period (a PDF needs the `fetch` extra), and appends one manual `boi.recorded` per matching row (an invoice belongs to the month holding most of its service period; Cartesia's plan invoice to `billing-coverage`, its overage invoice to `overage`) with the document as its evidence blob. A re-run of the same invoice appends nothing. A row with no invoice for the month, an unreadable document, two different invoices, or a currency other than the client's is reported on its row with its prefilled manual command; nothing is ever guessed or recorded as zero. Refused: `FETCHER_UNKNOWN`, `BROWSER_UNAVAILABLE` (no Kapture, not signed in), `FETCH_FAILED` (nothing recorded; its `next_command` is the manual line), `ACTOR_UNRESOLVED`.

| flag | type | required | help |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--client` | str | yes | Client slug. |
| `--vendor` | str | yes | A vendor with a fetcher: cartesia. |
| `--period` | str | yes | Calendar month YYYY-MM (UTC). |
| `--resource-id` | str | no | Only this one of the vendor's rows (plan or overage). |
| `--apply` | flag | no | Drive the browser (Kapture), download the invoice and record it as a manual boi with the document as evidence. |
| `--json` | flag | no | Print one JSON line: {"ok": true, "data": ...} or an error. |

`--json` data:

`FetchPlan`:
- `kind`: str
- `command`: str
- `steps`: list[PlannedStep]
- `apply_hint`: str
- `client`: str
- `vendor`: str
- `period_start`: date
- `period_end`: date
- `start_url`: str
- `rows`: list[FetchRowPlan]
- `apply_command`: str
`FetchApplied`:
- `kind`: str
- `client`: str
- `vendor`: str
- `period_start`: date
- `period_end`: date
- `documents_read`: int
- `documents_unreadable`: int
- `rows`: list[FetchedRow]
- `notes`: list[str]

## `ms category accept`

Create the proposed category: the one way a category is made.

Side effects: WRITES the ledger: OPERATOR ONLY. Appends one `category.added` naming the proposal (`p<seq>`): the way a proposal becomes a category. `--name`, `--description` and `--kind` override the proposed ones; a reason is required. The question set Jev is asked with changes, so transactions it declined are asked again. Refused: `PROPOSAL_UNKNOWN`, `PROPOSAL_CLOSED`, `CATEGORY_INVALID`, `REASON_REQUIRED`.

| flag | type | required | help |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<proposal>` | str | yes | The proposal id (p<seq>) `ms category list` shows. |
| `--name` | str | no | Use this name instead of the proposed one. |
| `--description` | str | no | Use this description instead. |
| `--kind` | one of: revenue, cogs, opex, owner, transfer | no | Use this kind (opex, cogs, ...). |
| `--reason` | str | no | Why; recorded with your actor. |
| `--json` | flag | no | Print one JSON line: {"ok": true, "data": ...} or an error. |

`--json` data:

`AcceptResult`:
- `category`: CatalogEntry
- `proposal`: str | null
- `seq`: int
- `question_set`: str

## `ms category add`

Create a category directly, with no proposal (an operator's path).

Side effects: WRITES the ledger: OPERATOR ONLY. Appends one `category.added` with no proposal: an operator's direct way to create a category Jev and a manual `ms tx tag` may then use. `--name`, `--kind` and `--description` (1 to 300 characters) are required, with a reason. The question set Jev is asked with changes, so transactions it declined are asked again. Refused: `CATEGORY_INVALID` (not a clean snake_case name, no description, or already active), `REASON_REQUIRED`.

| `--reason` | str | no | Why; recorded with your actor. |
| `--json` | flag | no | Print one JSON line: {"ok": true, "data": ...} or an error. |

## `ms category propose`

Suggest categories for repeated no-fit transactions. A plan unless --apply is given.

Side effects: PLAN by default: the counterparty groups with at least `MILKSHAKE_CATEGORY_PROPOSE_MIN` (default 3) untagged no-fit transactions and no open or rejected proposal; calls nothing and appends nothing. With `--apply` it asks the AAI gateway (its own consumer token, `MILKSHAKE_CATEGORY_LLM_TOKEN`, through `mise run ms --`) to name one category per group and appends one `category.proposed` (the exchange is an evidence blob). It never creates a category: only `category accept` does. A gateway failure is reported per group and records nothing, but a token that is not a usable consumer token refuses the whole run (`CATEGORY_NAMER_FAILED`, exit 3). At most 5 groups are named per run; `skipped_groups` counts the rest for the next run. Refused: `CATEGORY_NAMER_UNCONFIGURED`.

| flag | type | required | help |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--apply` | flag | no | Ask the AAI gateway to name each group's category and record it. |
| `--json` | flag | no | Print one JSON line: {"ok": true, "data": ...} or an error. |

`--json` data:

`ProposePlan`:
- `kind`: str
- `question_set`: str
- `minimum`: int
- `groups`: list[NoFitGroup]
- `waiting_no_fit`: int
- `credential_env`: str
- `credential_present`: bool
- `apply_hint`: str
`ProposeResult`:
- `kind`: str
- `proposed`: list[ProposalRow]
- `notes`: list[ProposeNote]
- `skipped_groups`: int

## `ms client set`

Change client fields (one client.updated event carrying only what changed).

Side effects: WRITES the ledger: appends one `client.updated` carrying only the changed fields. `--inference-pricing product` (Story 7.5) sells the client's llm charges at the gateway list from `--effective-from` (default today; never an earlier period); while the client forbids markup it needs `--contract-ref` (`CONTRACT_REF_REQUIRED`), and a flip to `--pass-through-markup forbidden` over a period a `product` setting without one still covers is refused the same way (date the flip and add `--inference-pricing pass_through`). `--mercury-customer` and `--revenue-counterparty` (Story 9.2) replace the client's Mercury identity: payment status, AR delivery and reconcile then find its cash by it instead of the one-customer fence. Refused: `MERCURY_ATTRIBUTION_CONFLICT` (another client names it).

| flag | type | required | help |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<slug>` | str | yes | The registered client slug. |
| `--legal-name` | str | no |  |
| `--billing-contact` | str | no |  |
| `--pass-through-markup` | one of: forbidden, allowed | no | Flip the contract guard; the flip itself is a ledger event. |
| `--contract-clause` | str | no | Clause the guard cites when it refuses; required when the client forbids markup (CONTRACT_CLAUSE_REQUIRED). |
| `--effective-from` | str | no | With --pass-through-markup or --inference-pricing: the first period start (YYYY-MM-DD) the change covers. Default: today for 'allowed' and for an inference change (never reaches an earlier period), every period for 'forbidden'. |
| `--inference-pricing` | one of: pass_through, product | no | 'product' sells llm charges at the gateway list (upstream x group ratio) under the Inference line, outside the pass-through guard; 'pass_through' (the default) prices them as a vendor cost. Dated with --effective-from. |
| `--contract-ref` | str | no | With --inference-pricing: the signed instrument behind it (e.g. 'Managed Platform Agreement s.2, signed 2026-12-01'). Required for 'product' while the client forbids markup (CONTRACT_REF_REQUIRED). |
| `--tax-treatment` | one of: not_collected, confirmed | no | 'confirmed' once the accountant has settled sales tax for this client (default 'not_collected'; ms shakedown warns tax_treatment_unconfirmed until then). Statements never carry a tax line either way. |
| `--tax-confirmed-by` | str | no | Who confirmed the tax treatment (with confirmed). |
| `--tax-confirmed-on` | str | no | Date of the confirmation, YYYY-MM-DD (default today, UTC). |
| `--mercury-customer` | str | no | The client's Mercury AR customer id (repeat for several; replaces the list). Its AR invoices and payments are then matched to it instead of the one-customer fence. |
| `--revenue-counterparty` | str | no | A name the client's payments arrive under in Mercury (whole words, any case; repeat for several; replaces the list). |
| `--json` | flag | no | Print one JSON line: {"ok": true, "data": ...} or an error. |

`--json` data:

`ClientResult`:
- `client`: Client
- `seq`: int | null
- `changed`: list[str]
- `markup_history`: list[MarkupChange]
- `inference_history`: list[InferenceChange]

## `ms farm export`

Write the canonical milkshake/v1 JSON snapshot (a query: nothing is appended).

Side effects: read-only: writes the `milkshake/v1` snapshot JSON file; appends no event. The snapshot carries what the Farm shows for the requested periods only: effective boi heads (and a head's reconciliation counterpart), never legacy imports or superseded revisions, plus per-period history counts. Every needs-input item carries its resolving `command` and `console_url`, every effective boi row its line-item `state` (Story 10.1). Refused: `FARM_GENERATED_AT_FUTURE` (`--generated-at` more than five minutes ahead).

| flag | type | required | help |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--client` | str | yes | Client slug. |
| `--period` | str | no | Calendar month YYYY-MM the snapshot covers: its effective bois, issued Yrds and a draft (repeatable, sorted and de-duplicated; default: the previous and the current month). |
| `--out` | path | no | File to write (with a suffix, e.g. snap.json), or a directory for farm.json (default: out/farm.json). |
| `--generated-at` | str | no | RFC 3339 instant to stamp (reproducible files); at most five minutes ahead of the clock. |
| `--json` | flag | no | Print one JSON line: {"ok": true, "data": ...} or an error. |

`--json` data:

`ExportResult`:
- `client`: str
- `path`: str
- `snapshot_schema`: str
- `generated_at`: datetime
- `payload_sha256`: str
- `head_seq`: int
- `head_hash`: str
- `periods`: list[str]
- `yrd_count`: int
- `bois_count`: int
- `rules_count`: int
- `blocking_count`: int

## `ms farm invoicer add`

Allow one email to ask the Farm to run commands for one client (plan or apply each).

Side effects: WRITES the ledger: appends one `farm.invoicer.added` (none when the grants are unchanged). OPERATOR ONLY. Grants one exact email, for ONE client, the allow-listed Farm commands it names (Story 10.3): `--plan-all` grants `plan` for every command that offers it (expanded now, never silently later) and `--grant "NAME=MODE"` (repeatable) adds or raises one, e.g. `--grant "squeeze=apply"`; `yrd issue=apply` is the old `--may-apply`, and `--may-accept-incomplete` needs it. `--client` is required (`FARM_GRANT_CLIENT_REQUIRED`): the legacy all-clients form can no longer be added. Re-adding replaces the client's grant. Refused: `FARM_GRANT_INVALID` (an unknown command, a mode it does not offer, an email over 158 characters), `FARM_GRANT_FORBIDDEN` (an agent address holding `apply` on an operator command). A domain (`@automaticai.io`) is refused. The portal's own allow-list can never widen this one.

| flag | type | required | help |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--email` | str | yes | The exact email (never a domain). |
| `--reason` | str | yes | Why this person may ask (recorded). |
| `--client` | str | no | The client the grant is for (required). |
| `--plan-all` | flag | no | Grant `plan` for every allow-listed command that offers it (expanded now; a command added later is never granted silently). |
| `--grant` | str | no | NAME=MODE, e.g. --grant "squeeze=apply" (repeatable; applied on top of --plan-all). NAME is an allow-listed command, MODE one it offers. |
| `--may-apply` | flag | no | Legacy: refused with --client. Use --grant "yrd issue=apply". |
| `--may-accept-incomplete` | flag | no | Also let them accept an incomplete statement (needs --grant "yrd issue=apply"). |
| `--json` | flag | no | Print one JSON line: {"ok": true, "data": ...} or an error. |

`--json` data:

`InvoicerResult`:
- `email`: str
- `client`: str | null
- `commands`: dict[str, GrantMode]
- `may_apply`: bool
- `may_accept_incomplete`: bool
- `changed`: bool
- `seq`: int | null

## `ms farm push`

Push the milkshake/v1 snapshot to the portal (a plan, no network call, unless --apply).

Side effects: OPERATOR ONLY (it publishes numbers to the client portal). PLAN by default: prints the endpoint (`${MILKSHAKE_FARM_URL:-https://www.automaticai.io}/api/milkshake-snapshot`), client, periods, `payload_sha256`, size and the diff against the last push; makes no network call and appends nothing. With `--apply` it POSTs the canonical snapshot once (`Authorization: Bearer $MILKSHAKE_FARM_TOKEN`, from `mise run ms --`) and, only on `{success: true}`, appends one `farm.pushed` (never the token). Idempotent: a repeat of the same bytes is the portal's `duplicate: true` and appends no second event; recording a push moves the ledger head, so retry with `--file` (the exact exported bytes). Refused before any request: `FARM_TOKEN_MISSING`, `FARM_TOKEN_INVALID` (under 32 characters, spaces or non-ASCII), `FARM_URL_INVALID`, `FARM_GENERATED_AT_FUTURE`, `FARM_SNAPSHOT_TOO_LARGE` (over the portal's 512 KB), `FARM_SNAPSHOT_INVALID`. Refused by the portal: `FARM_PUSH_UNAUTHORIZED`, `FARM_PUSH_FORBIDDEN`, `FARM_PUSH_CONFLICT`, `FARM_PUSH_INVALID`, `FARM_PUSH_REJECTED`, `FARM_PUSH_UNAVAILABLE`.

| flag | type | required | help |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--client` | str | no | Client slug (required unless --file is given). |
| `--period` | str | no | Calendar month YYYY-MM the snapshot covers (repeatable; default: the previous and the current month). |
| `--generated-at` | str | no | RFC 3339 instant to stamp (pins the exact bytes); at most five minutes ahead of the clock. |
| `--file` | path | no | Re-send the exact bytes of an earlier `ms farm export` (a byte-for-byte idempotent retry) instead of building a new snapshot. |
| `--apply` | flag | no | POST it to the portal and record farm.pushed (default: a plan). |
| `--json` | flag | no | Print one JSON line: {"ok": true, "data": ...} or an error. |

- `snapshot_schema`: 'milkshake/v1'

## `ms ledger reproject`

Rebuild the Postgres money projections from the events and prove them equal to the fold, or with --check only compare them (exit 5 on drift). A no-op on SQLite. Appends nothing.

Side effects: OPERATOR ONLY to rebuild; `--check` is read-only. On Postgres the `money` tables (clients, vendor rows, line items, rules, statements, payments, transactions, tags, categories) are projections of the ledger, kept equal to `fold` inside every append transaction. `--check` compares them with the fold from one snapshot and writes nothing; any difference (a missing, extra or changed row, a projection behind the head, or a missing `money` schema) is `PROJECTION_DRIFT`, exit 5. Without it the tables are rebuilt from the events under the writer's lock and the rebuild is proved equal to the fold. Appends no event; no statement or verify reads the tables. A no-op on SQLite.

| flag | type | required | help |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--check` | flag | no | Compare the projections with the fold and write nothing; exit 5 on any difference (default: rebuild them). |
| `--json` | flag | no | Print one JSON line: {"ok": true, "data": ...} or an error. |

`--json` data:

`ReprojectReport`:
- `mode`: 'check' | 'rebuild'
- `engine`: 'sqlite' | 'postgresql'
- `projected`: bool

- `head_seq`: int
- `head_hash`: str
- `watermark_seq`: int | null
- `projection_version`: int
- `clean`: bool
- `rows_written`: int
- `rows_deleted`: int
- `tables`: list[TableDrift]
- `note`: str | null

## `ms portfolio`

Every client's billed, client-borne and AAI-borne cost, margin, fees, kept and unpaid.

Side effects: read-only: one row per registered client for the month: each active issued statement overlapping it (the figures frozen at issue, with its payment status and unpaid remainder from the last recorded `ms yrd payment` check), or else the client's draft at the ledger head (with its blocking count). Per row: billed, client-borne and AAI-borne cost, margin, fees, discount and kept (billed less every vendor cost; negative when AAI subsidises the client); totals per currency, with `unpaid_unknown` counting statements whose payment was never checked (unknown is never 0). Calls no vendor and no bank; appends no event.

| flag | type | required | help |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--period` | str | yes | The calendar month, YYYY-MM. |
| `--at` | str | no | Judge drafts and due dates at this RFC 3339 instant instead of now. |
| `--json` | flag | no | Print one JSON line: {"ok": true, "data": ...} or an error. |

`--json` data:

`Portfolio`:
- `period_start`: date
- `period_end`: date
- `as_of_seq`: int
- `now`: datetime
- `rows`: list[PortfolioRow]
- `totals`: list[PortfolioTotals]
- `note`: str

## `ms pricing simulate`

Price real months under hypothetical models, in memory: client total, AAI cost, AAI margin and margin per model and month; the contract guard is reported, not applied (read-only).

Side effects: read-only: prices the client's real months under each `--model` in memory (the TUI preview mechanism: the client's pricing rules set aside, the model's rules added, folded, never written) and reports per model and month the client total, AAI cost (client-borne and AAI-borne), AAI margin and margin. | `--json` | flag | no | Print one JSON line: {"ok": true, "data": ...} or an error. |

## `ms reconcile`

Compare Mercury cash with accrued bois per vendor (read-only; never summed).

Side effects: read-only: GETs Mercury (cached under `$MILKSHAKE_HOME/runtime/mercury/`, atomically) and compares cash settled with accrued bois per vendor. It appends no event, writes no boi and alters no Yrd; cash and accrual are never summed. Needs `MILKSHAKE_MERCURY_API_KEY` (run through `mise run ms -- reconcile`) unless a cached read exists. A client that names its own Mercury identity (`ms client set C --mercury-customer ID --revenue-counterparty NAME`) is reconciled on its own cash (transactions the ledger tags as its own, payments from its own payer; `attribution: client`, `unattributed_cash` counting what is left out) and the one-customer fence does not apply to it. Any other client keeps the fence, which counts only the AR customers no other client claims and leaves out transactions tagged as, or sent by the payer of, another client (`other_clients_cash`); once another client is registered it also leaves out untagged money in (`unattributed_cash`: only `ms tx tag` makes it the client's), and it refuses while two clients name no Mercury identity.

| flag | type | required | help |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--client` | str | yes | Client slug. |
| `--period` | str | no | Calendar month YYYY-MM (UTC). |
| `--from` | str | no | Range start YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `--to` | str | no | Range end YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. |
| `--refresh` | flag | no | Re-read Mercury instead of using the cache. |
| `--json` | flag | no | Print one JSON line: {"ok": true, "data": ...} or an error. |

`--json` data:

`ReconcileReport`:
- `client`: str
- `period_start`: date
- `period_end`: date
- `as_of_seq`: int
- `cash_read_at`: datetime
- `note`: str
- `fence_ar_customers`: int
- `vendors`: list[VendorLine]
- `cash_buckets`: dict[str, int]
- `in_flight`: int
- `unmapped`: list[str]
- `known_errors_fixed`: list[str]
- `attribution`: str | null
- `unattributed_cash`: int | null
- `other_clients_cash`: int | null

## `ms squeeze`

Read each api row's vendor cost. A plan unless --apply is given.

Side effects: PLAN by default (no call, no event). With `--apply` it calls the vendors, appends `boi.recorded` for new readings and one `squeeze.completed`. Readers of current state only (cloudflare subscriptions, the openrouter meter) serve the open calendar month; a closed month or a range is `RangeUnsupported`, listed under `skipped` in the plan with no call (record it with `ms boi add --manual`). With `MILKSHAKE_REDIS_URL` set, a non-metered row read within `MILKSHAKE_CACHE_TTL_S` (six hours) and still the newest reading on the ledger is `cached`: no call, no boi, no outcome; `--refresh` bypasses and overwrites it. AWS keeps its ledger-derived window. A Redis failure is a miss, never an error.

| `--to` | str | no | Range end YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. |
| `--vendor` | str | no | Only this vendor. |
| `--refresh` | flag | no | Re-call metered rows read inside the cache window, and bypass (then overwrite) the read cache (MILKSHAKE_REDIS_URL). |
| `--apply` | flag | no | Call the vendors and record the readings. |
| `--json` | flag | no | Print one JSON line: {"ok": true, "data": ...} or an error. |

## `ms tui`

The dial board: shakedown, statement, rules and a slash palette that builds and previews each `ms` change before it is recorded. Needs the tui extra and a terminal; --json prints the board as data.

Side effects: OPERATOR TOOL, interactive: an agent has no terminal and never runs it (without a terminal it exits `TUI_NEEDS_TERMINAL`). With `--json` it is read-only: the board (shakedown, Yrd lines, the operator charges with their winning rule ids, rules, the contract guard) as one line, nothing written. In the terminal it is a dial board: a slash palette (`/bill_to`, `/split`, `/margin`, `/narrative`, `/adjust`, `/review`, `/revoke`) builds the exact `ms` command and previews its effect in memory; nothing is recorded until the operator stages and confirms, and then each change goes through the same command the CLI runs (one event each, attributed to `MILKSHAKE_ACTOR`; the contract guard still refuses a margin). Under `MILKSHAKE_READONLY` it explores and applying is refused `LEDGER_READONLY`. Needs the `tui` extra (`TUI_EXTRA_MISSING`).

## `ms tx categorize`

Jev tags what the vendor map could not. A plan unless --apply is given.

Side effects: PLAN by default: the untagged transactions the vendor map says nothing about (what Jev would be asked, at most `MILKSHAKE_JEV_MAX_REQUESTS`), the question-set version and the thresholds; calls nothing and appends nothing. With `--apply` it sends one System One request per transaction (a `choice` over the full category list plus a companion `noul` 'does any listed category fit') to `https://jev.delo.sh/typesafe/v1/systemone` with the `milkshake` virtual key (`MILKSHAKE_JEV_TOKEN`, through `mise run ms --`) before the ledger transaction opens, then records each answer: above both thresholds (`MILKSHAKE_JEV_CHOICE_THRESHOLD_BPS` 80%, `MILKSHAKE_JEV_FIT_THRESHOLD_BPS` 50%) one `tx.tagged` (`source=jev`, AAI's, the category's kind, the probability as the confidence, the question-set version and the exact answers as an evidence blob); otherwise one `tx.unfit` and the transaction stays untagged with its `ms tx tag` command (needs review). Answers are cached by the state's sha256 and the question set when Redis is configured. A Jev failure never blocks a sync or a tag: a request that gets no usable answer is reported and nothing is recorded for it (three failures in a row stop the run). Refused: `JEV_UNCONFIGURED`, `JEV_TOKEN_INVALID`.

| `--json` | flag | no | Print one JSON line: {"ok": true, "data": ...} or an error. |

## `ms tx push`

Write tags back to Mercury as a category and a note. A plan unless --apply is given.

Side effects: OPERATOR ONLY, and never from a timer, cron or agent. PLAN by default: for every tagged transaction whose newest tag is not on Mercury yet, the exact `PATCH /transaction/{id}` (`categoryId` and the structured note `ms:client=<slug|aai> kind=<kind> [line=<line>] tag=<seq>`, after whatever a person wrote there, as the ledger last synced it) and the Mercury custom categories it needs; calls nothing and appends nothing. With `--apply` it uses `MILKSHAKE_MERCURY_WRITE_TOKEN` (a token value of its own, never the read key's): `GET /categories`, `POST /categories` for each missing one, then per transaction a read of its current note (kept as Mercury holds it, never cut) and one PATCH, each confirmed write recorded as `tx.pushed` so a re-run sends only what changed. A write whose outcome is unknown (no answer, a 5xx or 408, a created category without an id, a note that could not be read) is `MERCURY_WRITE_UNCONFIRMED` (exit 5: look in Mercury; what was confirmed first is already recorded); a transaction Mercury refuses (a 4xx) or whose note is too long to keep does not stop the others and ends as `MERCURY_WRITE_FAILED` (exit 3). A projection of the tags: it changes no tag, charge or cash. Refused: `MERCURY_WRITE_TOKEN_INVALID`.

| flag | type | required | help |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--period` | str | no | Calendar month YYYY-MM (UTC, Mercury's createdAt). |
| `--apply` | flag | no | Write to Mercury: create missing categories, PATCH category and note (MILKSHAKE_MERCURY_WRITE_TOKEN). |
| `--json` | flag | no | Print one JSON line: {"ok": true, "data": ...} or an error. |

`--json` data:

`PushPlan`:
- `kind`: str
- `period_start`: date | null
- `period_end`: date | null
- `items`: list[PushItem]
- `categories`: list[str]
- `requests`: list[PlannedRequest]
- `already_pushed`: int
- `credential_env`: str
- `credential_present`: bool
- `apply_hint`: str
- `never_summed`: str
`PushResult`:
- `kind`: str
- `pushed`: list[Pushed]
- `created_categories`: list[str]
- `pending`: int
- `not_sent`: int
- `halt`: Halt | null
- `never_summed`: str

## `ms yrd issue`

Issue the Yrd under the gate: freeze its boi ids, rule ids, lines and HTML (operators).

Side effects: OPERATOR ONLY. PLAN by default: runs the issue gate and prints the number, total and what would be frozen, appending nothing (exit 3 or 4 when `--apply` would be refused). With `--apply` it appends one `yrd.issued` (frozen document, `content_sha256`, the customer HTML as a blob, any `--supersedes` link and any `--accept-incomplete` override). `--projected --reason R` issues a month that is still open: estimates, partial and stale readings are billed at their monthly run-rate (the plan prints every reading's math and what is left for the true-up), and the customer sees one plain note; refused for a closed period (`PROJECTED_PERIOD_INVALID`), exclusive with `--accept-incomplete`. Agents plan and report; they never apply.

| flag | type | required | help |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--client` | str | yes | Client slug. |
| `--period` | str | no | Calendar month YYYY-MM (UTC). |
| `--from` | str | no | Range start YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `--to` | str | no | Range end YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. |
| `--supersedes` | str | no | Issue the next version replacing this Yrd number. |
| `--force-reissue` | str | no | With --supersedes: reissue although nothing is stale; why. |
| `--number-tag` | str | no | Number series for this client (AAI-<TAG>-2026-10): needed when another client already holds the bare number for the period; later statements keep it. |
| `--with-pdf` | flag | no | Also render a PDF from the frozen HTML and store it with its sha256 (needs the pdf extra; without it nothing is issued). |
| `--accept-incomplete` | flag | no | Accept an immaterial client-borne residual (needs --reason and --approved-by). |
| `--projected` | flag | no | Issue an open month as a projection: estimates and partial readings at their monthly run-rate, rows with no money left for `ms yrd true-up` (needs --reason; not with --accept-incomplete). |
| `--reason` | str | no | Why the residual is accepted, or why the month is projected. |
| `--approved-by` | str | no | Who approved the override (recorded). |

## `ms yrd list`

List the issued Yrds: number, status, period, total, sha256, dates, any override.

Side effects: read-only: issued Yrds (number, status, period, total, sha256, dates, override). `--with-payment` also reads Mercury (GET only) and adds paid / partial / open / overdue per Yrd with the matching transaction ids (`unknown` without a credential, exit 0).

| flag | type | required | help |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--client` | str | no | Only this client. |
| `--with-payment` | flag | no | Add paid / partial / open / overdue from Mercury cash (reads Mercury, GET only; `unknown` without MILKSHAKE_MERCURY_API_KEY). |
| `--cached` | flag | no | With --with-payment: use the last cached Mercury read. |
| `--at` | str | no | Judge overdue at this RFC 3339 instant (reproducible). |
| `--json` | flag | no | Print one JSON line: {"ok": true, "data": ...} or an error. |

`--json` data:

`ListYrdsResult`:
- `as_of_seq`: int
- `yrds`: list[YrdSummary]
- `payment_origin`: 'live' | 'cache' | 'none' | null
- `payment_note`: str | null

## `ms yrd payment`

Poll Mercury (GET only) for payment of issued Yrds: paid, partial (with the remainder), open or overdue, with the matching transaction ids. Recorded as an event only on change.

Side effects: PLAN by default: polls Mercury (GET only: transactions and AR invoices) and prints the payment state of one issued Yrd (or all): paid, partial with the remainder in cents, open or overdue, with the matching transaction ids; appends nothing. With `--apply` it appends one `yrd.payment_changed` per Yrd whose state changed since the last one recorded (a repeat poll appends nothing). Payment is judged from cash, never from the AR invoice status; cash is never added to an accrual figure.

| flag | type | required | help |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<number>` | str | no | Yrd number; omit for every issued Yrd. |
| `--client` | str | no | Only this client's Yrds. |
| `--cached` | flag | no | Use the last cached Mercury read, no network. |
| `--at` | str | no | Judge overdue at this RFC 3339 instant (reproducible). |
| `--apply` | flag | no | Append yrd.payment_changed where the state changed (default: a plan). |
| `--json` | flag | no | Print one JSON line: {"ok": true, "data": ...} or an error. |

`--json` data:

`PaymentReport`:
- `as_of_seq`: int
- `origin`: 'live' | 'cache' | 'none'
- `read_at`: datetime | null
- `note`: str | null
- `never_summed`: str
- `payments`: list[PaymentRow]
`RecordPaymentResult`:
- `kind`: str
- `origin`: str
- `read_at`: datetime | null
- `never_summed`: str
- `payments`: list[RecordedPayment]
- `recorded_count`: int

## `ms yrd render`

Render a statement to one file and print its sha256: an issued Yrd by number (its frozen HTML, or as PDF), else the draft for --client and a period.

Side effects: read-only: writes the draft HTML file and prints its sha256; appends no event.

| flag | type | required | help |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<number>` | str | no | An issued Yrd number (AAI-2026-10): render that statement from its frozen HTML. Without it, --client and a period render a draft. |
| `--client` | str | no | Client slug (a draft). |
| `--period` | str | no | Calendar month YYYY-MM (UTC). |
| `--from` | str | no | Range start YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `--to` | str | no | Range end YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive. |
| `--view` | one of: customer, operator | no | customer (what the client receives) or operator (internal: every boi and rule). |
| `--format` | one of: html, pdf | no | html (default) or pdf (needs the pdf extra; from the frozen HTML for a number). |
| `--out` | path | no | File to write (has a suffix, e.g. x.pdf), or a directory for the default name (e.g. AAI-2026-10.pdf, or AAI-2026-10.draft.html for a draft; default: out/). |
| `--at` | str | no | Judge staleness at this RFC 3339 instant (operator view). |
| `--json` | flag | no | Print one JSON line: {"ok": true, "data": ...} or an error. |

`--json` data:

`RenderResult`:
- `view`: View
- `format`: Format
- `number`: str
- `status`: str
- `as_of_seq`: int
- `path`: str
- `sha256`: str
- `size_bytes`: int
- `source`: 'draft' | 'frozen_html' | 'stored_pdf'
- `ledger_pdf_sha256`: str | null

## `ms yrd true-up`

Settle a projected Yrd: actual minus what was billed per customer label, once the period has closed and every client-borne reading is final; settles again when figures moved after a settlement (operators).

Side effects: OPERATOR ONLY. PLAN by default: settles a projected Yrd, computing actual (a build at the head) minus projected per customer label and printing the adjustment lines, appending nothing. With `--apply` it appends one `yrd.trued_up` (`--into next`, the default: the next statement carries the lines; `--into one-off`: a separate `NUMBER-TU` statement is also issued) and the projected Yrd is settled. Refused while a client-borne reading is still provisional or missing (`TRUE_UP_READINGS_PENDING`, exit 4, naming each with its command), before the close (`PERIOD_OPEN`), for a Yrd that was not projected, is superseded or is already settled.

| flag | type | required | help |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<number>` | str | yes | The projected Yrd to settle (AAI-2026-10; `ms yrd list`). |
| `--into` | one of: next, one-off | no | next (default): adjustment lines on the next statement; one-off: a separate NUMBER-TU statement with only the adjustment lines. |
| `--reason` | str | no | Why (recorded; the next operator reads it). |
| `--apply` | flag | no | Record it: append yrd.trued_up (default: a plan). |
| `--json` | flag | no | Print one JSON line: {"ok": true, "data": ...} or an error. |

`--json` data:

`TrueUpOutcome`:
- `kind`: 'plan' | 'applied'
- `command`: str
- `apply_hint`: str
- `steps`: list[PlannedStep]
- `number`: str
- `client`: str
- `into`: TrueUpInto
- `period_start`: date
- `period_end`: date
- `carry_start`: date | null
- `carry_end`: date | null
- `as_of_seq`: int
- `lines`: list[TrueUpLine]
- `net_cents`: int
- `nothing_to_settle`: bool
- `issued_number`: str | null
- `content_sha256`: str | null
- `html_sha256`: str | null
- `seq`: int | null

## `ms yrd verify`

Replay the issue from the ledger and prove it reproduces content_sha256 (exit 5 if not).

Side effects: read-only: replays `evaluate` and `project` at the recorded `as_of_seq` and proves the frozen document reproduces `content_sha256` (a projected Yrd replays with its frozen projection inputs, proved against the ledger first; a settled one also recomputes its true-up); exit 5 (`YRD_HASH_MISMATCH`) if not.

| flag | type | required | help |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `<number>` | str | yes | Yrd number, e.g. AAI-2026-10. |
| `--json` | flag | no | Print one JSON line: {"ok": true, "data": ...} or an error. |

`--json` data:

`VerifyYrdResult`:
- `number`: str
- `ok`: bool
- `content_sha256`: str
- `recomputed_sha256`: str
- `as_of_seq`: int
- `html_sha256`: str
- `pdf_sha256`: str | null
- `status`: 'issued' | 'superseded'
- `template_drift`: bool
- `not_covered`: list[str]
- `basis`: str | null
- `settled_by`: int | null
